;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2019 Indanan bombings]]
**Two suicide bombers detonate their devices in [[Sulu]], [[Philippines]], killing four soldiers and two civilians. [[Abu Sayyaf|ISIL]] claims responsibility. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/explosion-southern-philippines-military-base-1.5194239 (CBC)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-philippines-security/philippine-army-camp-blast-kills-five-islamic-state-claims-responsibility-idUSKCN1TT1T6 (Reuters)] [https://www.cnnphilippines.com/regional/2019/6/29/sulu-twin-blasts-death-toll.html (CNN Philippines)]
*[[Syrian Civil War]], [[Northwestern Syria offensive (April 2019–present)]]
**Nearly 100 people are killed in clashes between the [[Syrian Army]], rebels and [[Hayat Tahrir al-Sham|jihadists]] in northwestern Syria. 51 government troops and allied militiamen, and 45 rebel fighters and jihadists are among the dead. [https://www.france24.com/en/20190628-nearly-100-dead-northwest-syria-fighting-monitor (France 24)]

;Business and economy
*Demolition experts implode the ''[[Ponte Morandi]]'' [[viaduct]] in [[Genoa]], [[Italy]], ten months after a partial collapse that killed 43 people. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/av/world-europe-48797883/morandi-bridge-towers-demolished-in-genoa (BBC News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*A train hauling 40 cars derails in the [[St. Clair Tunnel]] between [[Port Huron, Michigan]] and [[Sarnia|Sarnia, Ontario]], spilling 13,700 gallons of [[sulfuric acid]] and closing the tunnel for several days. [https://www.clickondetroit.com/news/train-derails-inside-st-clair-river-international-tunnel-in-port-huron (WDIV-TV)] [https://www.wxyz.com/news/19-rail-cars-remain-inside-international-st-clair-river-tunnel-after-derailment-last-week (WXYZ-TV)]

;International relations
*[[China–Holy See relations]]
**The Vatican asks China's communist government to stop intimidating [[Catholics in China|Catholic]] clergy who want to remain unequivocally loyal to the pope and refuse to sign ambiguous official registration forms. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pope-china/vatican-says-china-intimidating-catholics-loyal-to-pope-idUSKCN1TT1MY (Reuters)]
*[[Bahrain–Iraq relations]]
**More than 200 demonstrators break into the courtyard of Bahrain's embassy in [[Baghdad]] and take down the kingdom's flag to protest a U.S.-led meeting in Bahrain on the [[Israeli–Palestinian peace process]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-israel-palestinians-plan-iraq/baghdad-protesters-take-down-bahrain-flag-over-trump-peace-conference-idUSKCN1TS359 (Reuters)]
*[[Foreign relations of Argentina]]
**[[Argentine Foreign Minister]] [[Jorge Faurie]] announces that the [[European Union]] and [[Argentina]], [[Brazil]], [[Paraguay]] and [[Uruguay]] achieved a breakthrough in free-trade talks after 20 years. [https://gulfnews.com/business/historic-eu-and-south-america-achieve-breakthrough-in-free-trade-talks-after-20-years-1.1561745528904 (''Gulf News'')]
*[[United States–Venezuela relations]]
**The [[United States]] announces sanctions on [[Nicolás Maduro Guerra]], the son of [[2019 Venezuelan presidential crisis|disputed]] [[President of Venezuela|Venezuelan President]] [[Nicolás Maduro]], accusing him of engaging in propaganda on behalf of the government. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-48805421 (BBC News)]
*[[2019 Argentine general election]], [[Argentina–Brazil relations]], [[Argentina–United States relations]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] and [[President of Brazil|Brazilian President]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]] officially endorse the re-election campaign of [[Mauricio Macri]]. [https://www.lanacion.com.ar/politica/fuerte-respaldo-trump-bolsonaro-macri-que-no-nid2262755 (''La Nación'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Salt Lake City]] [[Salt Lake City Police Department|police]] arrest a man for murder in connection to the search for missing [[University of Utah]] student Mackenzie Lueck. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/missing-university-utah-student-one-man-custody-salt-lake-city-n1024631 (NBC News)]
*Aftermath of the [[Charlottesville car attack]]
**James A. Fields Jr. is sentenced to life in prison after pleading guilty to 29 hate crimes for driving his car into a crowd of protestors, killing one and injuring 28, at the 2017 [[Unite the Right rally]] in [[Charlottesville, Virginia]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/06/28/us/charlottesville-car-attacker-sentencing/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/james-alex-fields-driver-deadly-car-attack-charlottesville-rally-sentenced-n1024436 (NBC News)] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/public-safety/james-fields-jr-avowed-neo-nazi-in-charlottesville-car-attack-set-to-be-sentenced-for-federal-hate-crimes/2019/06/27/fcead458-9849-11e9-830a-21b9b36b64ad_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[Capital punishment in Sri Lanka]]
**For the first time in 43 years, [[Sri Lanka]] hires executioners to reinstate the [[death penalty]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/jun/28/sri-lanka-appoints-executioners-for-return-of-death-penalty-after-40-years (''The Guardian'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Immigration to Japan]]
**A [[Nigerians in Japan|Nigerian]] man dies in a Japanese immigration detention center this week, an official says. It ends a hunger strike that an activist group said was intended to protest against him being held for more than three years. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-japan-immigration-hunger-strike/nigerian-man-dies-after-hunger-strike-in-japan-detention-center-idUSKCN1TT0R4 (Reuters)]
*The [[House of Representatives (Netherlands)|House of Representatives of the Netherlands]] passes the final bill of the climate agreement. The goal of the accord is to have the level of greenhouse gasses in the atmosphere in 2030 the same as the level of greenhouse gasses in the atmosphere in 1990. [https://abcnews.go.com/Technology/wireStory/dutch-government-presents-measures-cut-carbon-emissions-64015905 (ABC News)]
*According to the first report presented by the [[Nicaraguan Foundation for Economic and Social Development]], [[Nicaragua]] has become one of the world's least democratic countries, qualifying it as an "authoritarian regime". Among the reasons that this center of thought mentions to explain this situation are "the retrocess of civil liberties by the repression against [[2018–2019 Nicaraguan protests|the anti-government protests in progress since 2018]]" and "the loss of independence of the State institutions in favor of the Executive Power". [https://www.laprensa.com.ni/2019/06/28/politica/2564900-nicaragua-esta-entre-los-paises-menos-democraticos-del-mundo-segun-funides (La Prensa)]

;Science and technology
*[[2019 European heat wave]]
**Amid a continental [[heat wave]], [[France]] records its highest ever temperature of {{convert|45.9|C|F}} in [[Gallargues-le-Montueux]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/europe-heatwave-france-raises-danger-alert-to-highest-level-11750609 (Sky News)]
**In [[Spain]], authorities report two deaths connected to the extreme heat. The worst wildfire in 20 years burns more than 5,000 hectares at the south of [[Province of Tarragona]], in [[Catalonia]]. [https://www.express.co.uk/news/world/1146431/spain-heatwave-weather-forecast-madrid-Cordoba (''Express'')] [https://www.cnn.com/2019/06/27/world/europe-heat-wave-spain-wildfire-intl/index.html (CNN)]
